title: Week Ahead — Week of Nov 9, 2026
html:
Here's what I'm seeing. Last week one ugly Thursday knocked SPY through its floor, and the money ran from AI into travel. This week brings the inflation report, more AI earnings and a Fed that is leaning toward a hike. Here's the game plan.

The one thing

SPY's line this week is $745 above and $722–728 below. Until it closes back above $745, keep trades small and favor the names that held up.

SPY closed Friday at $735.29, down 2.7% for the week, after Thursday's 4.4% drop, the worst day since April 2025. Chips fell 11–12% that day on worries that the new Congress will limit data-center building. Friday's bounce stalled at $742.21, just under the old floor at $744–745, which is now acting as a ceiling. Futures put about 80% odds on a December rate hike after a hot jobs report (165K jobs against about 70K expected). A close above $745 after CPI says the scare is over. A close below $722 breaks the uptrend, and then cash is a position.

SPY in one picture

Two Fib levels from different swings tell the story. The 23.6% retracement of the big March–October run ($744.92) is the floor that broke on Thursday. Below us, the 200-day average ($727.65) and the 38.2% retracement of that same run ($722.22) sit together. When two levels land close to each other, we call it confluence, and that zone matters more than either line alone.

  • Oct 6 record high: $781.62
  • Ceiling · 61.8% + 20- & 50-day: $763–765
  • 38.2–50% of the Oct–Nov drop: $751–757
  • The line · old floor, now ceiling: $744–745
  • NOW $735.29
  • Shelf · Nov 5 low + 1.382 ext: $732.5
  • Big floor · 200-day + 38.2% of big run: $722–728
  • 50% of the Mar–Oct run: $703.87

How I read it: this is a pullback inside an uptrend, not a downtrend yet, because SPY is still above its 200-day. What changes my view: a close above $745 turns me constructive (the SPY call trigger); a close below $722 means the uptrend is broken.

The week, day by day

  • Mon (Quiet): No big data. Rocket Lab, Take-Two and Trump Media report after the close. The intraday check will look at DAL and PLTR, but if one triggers before CPI, keep it to one contract.
  • Tue (Big day): CPI, the inflation report, at 8:30 a.m. Forecasts: prices +0.3% for the month (last time +0.6%), core +0.2%. A hot number makes a December hike close to certain and hits growth stocks. CoreWeave reports after the close, a read on AI spending.
  • Wed (Holiday): Veterans Day. Stocks are open, the bond market is closed, so volume is usually light.
  • Thu (Big day): Cisco, Applied Materials and Cerebras report after the close (Nebius before the open). This is the chip read-through for SMH, MU and AMD. Weekly jobless claims at 8:30 (forecast 194K).
  • Fri (Data): PPI, wholesale inflation, at 8:30 a.m. (forecast +0.4%, core +0.3%). Three Fed speakers: Collins, Bowman and Daly.

Further out: Nvidia reports and retail sales come Nov 17, the Fed minutes Nov 18, Dell reports Nov 24. The Fed meets Dec 8–9. See Fed Tracker and Federal Reserve.

Which themes are winning

  • Travel & hotels (ABNB · DAL · RCL · HLT) — 76/100: Winning. ABNB +15.6% on earnings, DAL +8.8%, RCL +6.5%. BA lags.
  • Defensive rotation (KO) — 66/100: KO hit a 52-week high ($97.39) while tech fell.
  • Mega-cap consumer & cloud (AAPL · AMZN · GOOGL) — 50/100: Split. AMZN +7.9%, AAPL flat, GOOGL in a downtrend (RSI 30).
  • Rates & a hiking Fed (TLT · IWM) — 40/100: About 80% odds of a December hike. IWM −2%, TLT flat. CPI decides.
  • Oil shock / Iran (XOM · XLE · USO) — 34/100: Cracking. Brent near $98, down about 12% on Iran talks. Good news for DAL and RCL.
  • Defense (LMT · BA) — 32/100: LMT −11% in a week; BA still in a downtrend.
  • Musk complex (TSLA · SPCX) — 28/100: TSLA −10.4%, back under its 200-day.
  • AI infrastructure (NVDA · MU · SMH · DELL · BE) — 18/100: Losing. MU −22%, DELL −22.6%, SMH −11.2%. Data-center limits are the new fear.
  • AI vs software (NOW · PLTR) — 15/100: NOW made a new low ($100.55). PLTR fell 12.9% but bounced off its 200-day.

Why these four: DAL is your main long and sits under its trigger; PLTR is your new tested setup; XOM is where your own Fib drawing is doing the talking; BA is the closest put trigger.

  • The chart: Uptrend: price and the 50-day are above the 200-day. RSI 61, healthy, not stretched. It is sitting on the 38.2% retracement of the July–October drop ($87.14).
  • Watching: A move above $88 at the intraday check triggers the $90 call. Targets: the 0.5 extension at $91.86, then the July high $95.18. Invalidation: a close below $83, or Brent back over $100.
  • Status: Ready on trigger. Your open $85 call is up about $215 on paper.

Lesson of the week: Cheap or expensive: comparing the price tag with how much the stock really moves

Every option has an implied volatility (IV) built into its price. It's the market's guess of how much the stock will move in a year. Realized volatility is what the stock has actually done, here measured over the last 60 trading days. Divide the first by the second and you know if you're overpaying: under 0.9 is cheap, 0.9–1.25 is fair, over 1.25 is expensive.

  • NOW Dec $102 put: ratio 0.61 — IV 50% vs moves 82% → CHEAP
  • NVDA Dec $170 put: ratio 1.45 — IV 59% vs moves 40% → EXPENSIVE, earnings inside

Why it matters: when an option is expensive, the stock has to move more just for you to break even. NVDA puts are priced for a bigger move than NVDA usually makes, and they include its Nov 17 earnings, so that extra premium vanishes after the report (IV crush). Cheap doesn't mean good, either: NOW puts are cheap because the stock is already down a lot and RSI is 28. The price tag is one check, not the reason to trade. This week's four plays are all FAIR, between 0.92 and 1.20.

Fib lesson of the week (Fibonacci Playbook): Runaway extensions: how your XOM drawing called the top and mapped the drop

Last week there was no chart assignment to check, so we start fresh. It's an extension week.

A 3-point extension projects a past swing forward. You take one move (A to B), then measure it again from a new point C: level = C + (B − A) × ratio. In your XOM drawing the swing is $20.42 (roughly the late-April low near $143.6 to the May high near $164.0) and C is $126.05. Please confirm your exact A/B/C dates next time.

The math: 3.0 → 126.05 + 3 × 20.42 = $187.31. 2.618 → 126.05 + 53.46 = $179.51. 2.382 → 126.05 + 48.64 = $174.69. 2.0 → 126.05 + 40.84 = $166.89. 1.618 → 126.05 + 33.04 = $159.09.

What price did: the big ratios (2.382 to 3.0) are where runaway moves run out of buyers. On Oct 30 XOM hit $188.50 and closed at $187.25, right on the 3.0. Then it closed under 2.618 on Nov 3 ($177.46), under 2.382 on Nov 4 ($169.27) and under 2.0 on Nov 5 ($165.30). Friday's high of $166.79 failed ten cents under the 2.0: old support turned resistance.

What it means for a trade: as long as XOM stays under $166.89, the next stops down are $159.09 and then $154.3, where the 1.382 meets the 200-day. That confluence is a buy zone to study, with the stop just beyond it, a close below about $152. A close back above $166.89 flips it; that would point to the Dec $170 call ($485, OI 9,861, IV 30% vs moves 27% → FAIR) aiming at $174.69. Neither is a play yet.

Level scorecard (last week's ladders): retracements held 3, broke 2, wick 0 (60% held). Extensions: none graded yet; XOM's levels start counting this week.

Ladder:

  • 3.0 = 126.05 + 3 × 20.42 (high $188.50): $187.31
  • 2.618: $179.51
  • 2.382: $174.69
  • 2.0 · the line now: $166.89
  • NOW $165.87
  • Nov 6 low: $163.51
  • 1.618 · next target down: $159.09
  • 1.382 (+ 200-day $154.46): $154.27
